label: Cat6a 24-port shielded feed-through patch panel, 1U
description: 1U 19-inch Cat6a shielded feed-through (coupler) patch panel, 24 RJ45 ports front and back, rated for 10GBASE-T and PoE++ (802.3bt). Physically passive: a mated front/rear pair is one connector junction, not a repeater. In the simulator each panel port terminates one link - the engine has no internal front-to-rear pass-through - so a panel models the patch point and its port budget, not a cabled-through path (see notes).
formFactor: 1U 19-inch, 24 x shielded Cat6a couplers, cable management bar included
notes: FS product 118904 / P/N C6AP-S24FT1U: 'Cat6a Coupler Patch Panel, 24-Port, 1RU', shielded feed-through modules, 'ideal for 10/100/1000Base-T and 10GBase-T Ethernet applications', 10GBase-T and PoE++ rated, cable management bar included; the same family also lists 48-port 2U punch-down variants. Categorised as splitter, matching the passive-panel convention already used for fs/FHD-1U-PP-24LC in this catalogue - there is no dedicated patch-panel category, and inventing one would break the category count assertions for a device that behaves like a passive panel. MODELLING LIMITATION, tested rather than assumed: cabled switch-port -> panel port1 succeeds, but panel port1 cannot then be connected onward ('d2/port1 is already connected'), because a port in this engine has exactly one link and there is no internal front-to-rear junction. So the panel is a patch point with 24 copper endpoints, not a cabled-through path; the same is true of the existing fibre panel. Making panels actually pass traffic needs an internal-pair concept in the engine (like the splitter's replication table), which is a design change, not device data. Ports carry the full copper ladder (100M-10G) so a panel never silently caps a 10G run.
